arxiv-2010-06003.description: Abstract Mobile devices with embedded sensors for data collection and environmental sensing create a basis for a cost-effective approach for data trading. For example, these data can be related to pollution and gas emissions, which can be used to check the compliance with national and international regulations.

arxiv-2209-09499.title: Compact objects in gravity theories
arxiv-2209-09499.creator: Athanasios Bakopoulos 2, Christos Charmousis 1 and Nicolas Lecoeur 1
arxiv-2209-09499.description: Abstract We briefly discuss explicit compact object solutions in higher-order scalar-tensor theories. We start by so-called stealth solutions, whose metric are General Relativity (GR) solutions, but accompanied by a non-trivial scalar field, in both spherically-symmetric and rotating cases. The latter then enables to construct an analytic stationary solution of scalar tensor theory which is called disformed Kerr metric.

arxiv-2506-15519.title: On balanced HKT manifolds
arxiv-2506-15519.creator: Giovanni Gentili, Mehdi Lejmi
arxiv-2506-15519.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Giovanni Gentili, Mehdi Lejmi. We prove the openness of the balanced HKT cone within the cone of HKT structures on a compact hypercomplex manifold ( M , I , J , K ) (M,I,J,K) . We also study the Lie algebra of hyperholomorphic vector fields of type ( 1 , 0 ) (1,0) with respect to I I , with particular emphasis on the case when there exists a compatible balanced HKT metric.

arxiv-2509-08684.creator: Alessandro De Luca, Gabriele Fici
arxiv-2509-08684.description: Abstract A binary word is Sturmian if the occurrences of each letter are balanced, in the sense that in any two factors of the same length, the difference between the number of occurrences of the same letter is at most 1 1 . In digital geometry, Sturmian words correspond to discrete approximations of straight line segments in the Euclidean plane.

pmc-11352539.title: Complex Interplay between DNA Damage and Autophagy in Disease and Therapy
pmc-11352539.creator: Aman Singh, Naresh Ravendranathan, Jefferson C Frisbee, Krishna K Singh, Da-Tian Bau, Shunbin Ning
pmc-11352539.description: Cancer, a multifactorial disease characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation, remains a global health challenge with significant morbidity and mortality. Genomic and molecular aberrations, coupled with environmental factors, contribute to its heterogeneity and complexity. Chemotherapeutic agents like doxorubicin (Dox) have shown efficacy against various cancers but are hindered by dose-dependent cytotoxicity, particularly on vital organs like the heart and brain.

pmc-11489174.title: Molecular changes in intraocular fluid: implications for myopia
pmc-11489174.creator: Zewei Zhang, Lingfeng Lv, Dongmei Chen, Fang Li, Jibo Zhou
pmc-11489174.description: Myopia is the most common eye disease in the world which is caused by a mismatch between the optical power of the eye and its excessive axial length. Scleral remodeling, oxidative stress, inflammation, pathological states of angiogenesis and fibrosis and metabolism are closely associated with the onset and progression of myopia and the pathological changes that may ultimately result.

pmc-12528197.description: IntroductionIdentification and treatment of neurological disorders depend much on brain imaging and neurotherapeutic decision support. pmc-12557238.title: COVID-19 school closures affect adolescents’ educational qualifications and post-school pathways
pmc-12557238.creator: JAC Penders, MWG Bosmans
pmc-12557238.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic caused widespread school closures, disrupting adolescents’ education at a critical phase. These disruptions raised concerns about diploma attainment and the transition to further education or employment. This study examines the impact of COVID-related school closures in the Netherlands on basic qualification attainment and post-school activities.

pmc-12583231.title: Alteration in Gastric Ghrelin Expression in a Mouse Model of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
pmc-12583231.creator: Minami Watanabe, Ippei Watari, Masato Akakura, Srisutha Jiratchaya, Takashi Ono
pmc-12583231.description: BackgroundGhrelin, produced and secreted in the stomach, stimulates appetite by acting on the hypothalamus and inhibits insulin secretion, leading to hyperglycemia. Ghrelin is also associated with obesity and insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Beyond metabolic regulation, ghrelin is linked to autophagy and oxidative stress, leading to many chronic inflammatory diseases.

pmc-12593652.title: Protocol for in vitro immunofluorescence staining in a Transwell co-culture system
pmc-12593652.creator: Jenny YY Ooi, Yung Shing Tsang, Lawrence P McMahon, Limy Wong
pmc-12593652.description: SummaryImmunofluorescence (IF) is a key technique for localizing target molecules. Here, we present a protocol for in vitro IF staining optimized for skeletal muscle myotube formation cultured on Transwell inserts. We describe steps for primary cell culture, fixing, permeabilization, and antibody incubation. We then detail procedures for quantifying myotube differentiation by IF microscopy to calculate fusion index.

pmc-12728234.title: Prevalence, Types and Contributing Factors of Female Infertility at Orotta National Referral Maternity Hospital, Eritrea: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-12728234.creator: Berhe Tesfai, Kibreab Mehari, Senay Tesfamichael Ghebregherghsh, Okbu Frezgi, Fitsum Kibreab
pmc-12728234.description: BackgroundFemale infertility is a distressing event to couples, and it is mainly caused by ovulatory disorders, pituitary gland dysfunction, fallopian tube blockage, and uterine abnormalities. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, risk factors, and types of female infertility among patients visiting Orotta National Referral Maternity Hospital.

pmc-12753870.title: A novel fully human anti-ROR1 antibody PBA-0405 optimized for ADCC, induces potent anti-tumor activity against both solid and hematological malignancies
pmc-12753870.creator: Niina Veitonmäki, Anna Kostyn, Sonia Kołt, Aleksandra Ziemblicka, Beata Romanowska, Sabina Oleksy, Ewelina Krzywińska, Kamilla Sołtys, Łukasz Świderski, Piotr Naporowski, Piotr Mamczur, Monika Świtoń, Marek Orłowski, Ying Zhang, Jianming Xu, Anna Andrzejczak, Aleksandra Bielawska-Pohl, Lidia Karabon
pmc-12753870.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionB-cell malignancies, including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), pose a significant clinical challenge due to high relapse rates and dose-limiting toxicities seen with current therapies, particularly in elderly patients. Receptor tyrosine kinase-like orphan receptor 1 (ROR1) is an attractive therapeutic target due to its high expression on malignant B-cells and minimal presence in normal adult tissues, allowing the development of more potent and safer drugs for cancer treatment.

pmc-12971007.title: Cerebral oxygen extraction and blood flow in community-based older adults: associations with white matter hyperintensity and neurocognitive function
pmc-12971007.creator: Yifan Yan, Xuhao Zhao, Yaping Zhang, Wanxin Li, Zhiying Lin, Yi Zhou, Shenghao Fang, Jingkai Huang, Christopher Li-Hsian Chen, Zixuan Lin, Xin Xu
pmc-12971007.description: Cerebral oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) and cerebral blood flow (CBF) are key haemodynamic markers. Emerging evidence suggests that they may exert compensatory effects on small vessel disease and cognitive outcomes, with potentially nonlinear relationships, particularly in community-dwelling seniors. Therefore, we conducted a cross-sectional study of 296 participants from the Heritage Study in China.

pmc-13303089.description: Amylin receptor agonists such as cagrilintide represent emerging obesity therapies. pmc-13625767.title: Dietary Perovskia abrotanoides essential oil and vitamin E improve performance, antioxidant status, and intestinal morphology in laying Japanese quails fed oxidized oil
pmc-13625767.creator: Nematullah Kordi Koosheh, Mohammad Taher Mirakzehi, Hassan Saleh, Tayebeh Baranzehi
pmc-13625767.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study investigated the effects of dietary oxidized oil, Perovskia abrotanoides essential oil (PAEO), and vitamin E (VE) on productive performance, egg quality, antioxidant status, intestinal morphology, and hepatic gene expression in laying Japanese quails. A total of 480 48-day-old quails were randomly assigned to 8 experimental groups (6 replicates of 10 birds each) in a factorial arrangement (2 × 2 × 2).

pmc-13655184.title: Perceived Labor Control Among Latinas: Examining the Role of Pregnancy Loss, Prenatal Depression, and Childbirth Pain Severity
pmc-13655184.creator: Sandraluz Lara‐Cinisomo, Biniyam Melesse
pmc-13655184.description: IntroductionPrenatal mental health, perception of pain, and pregnancy histories can affect a birthing person's sense of control during labor. Although recent research has focused on cesarean births, less attention has been given to the role those factors play in perceived control during vaginal births.
